newsitem.title: UK: British firm to release "lost" Glenn Miller tapes.
newsitem.headline: British firm to release "lost" Glenn Miller tapes.

text.p: U.S. researchers have found a batch of previously unknown recordings by U.S. wartime bandleader Glenn Miller, many of which will be released next week, a British music company said on Thursday.
A spokeswoman for BMG Conifer said 22 sessions of 15 minutes each, many of which featured backing by a 21-piece string section, was discovered recently in U.S. military archives.
Miller and his band recorded the material, which was distributed to foreign radio stations to be used for propaganda purposes, between March and June 1944 in the United States, the spokeswoman said.

BMG will release 227 minutes of the sessions on Monday under the title of "The Secret Broadcasts" in a triple set of compact discs or cassettes. An album of rediscovered Miller recordings released last year, entitled "Glenn Miller - The Lost Recordings", sold more than 400,000 copies worldwide.

The recordings, broadcast to German troops on a U.S. wartime propaganda radio station as "Music for the Wehrmacht", were finished in London just weeks before Miller's plane vanished over the English Channel in December 1944.
Jazz and swing were banned in Nazi Germany where they were depicted as the decadent art form of an inferior race.
